question: What is the primary purpose of a physical examination in clinical practice?

options.A: To replace the need for a patient health history
options.C: To prescribe medication without a doctor present
options.D: To evaluate a patient's overall health status

explanation: A physical examination provides objective data about a patient's body systems to evaluate their current health. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why is physical examination especially vital in rural primary health care settings?

options.A: It compensates for a complete lack of patient history
options.B: Advanced laboratory machines are always readily available
options.C: It serves as a primary tool when diagnostics are limited
options.D: It eliminates the need for any formal nursing documentation

explanation: Clinicians rely heavily on physical assessment findings when diagnostic equipment is sparse or unavailable. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why should a patient empty their bladder before an abdominal physical examination?

options.A: To prevent discomfort and inaccurate palpation findings
options.B: To stop the patient from moving during inspection
options.C: To allow the collection of a sterile urine specimen
options.D: To reduce the total duration of the nursing shift

explanation: A full bladder can cause patient discomfort and make deep palpation of abdominal organs difficult or misleading. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h2)

question: What environmental factor is most critical for successful auscultation of lung sounds?

options.B: A quiet room with minimal background noise
options.C: An open window for steady fresh airflow
options.D: Low humidity and cool ambient temperature

explanation: Quiet surroundings are necessary to hear subtle breath or heart sounds through a stethoscope. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h2)

question: When should a nurse perform hand hygiene during a physical examination?

options.A: Before and after direct contact with every patient
options.B: Only after touching visible blood or body fluids
options.C: At the beginning of the morning shift and at noon
options.D: Only when leaving the examination room entirely

explanation: Hand hygiene breaks the chain of infection and must be performed before and after every patient interaction. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which action violates standard infection control practices during a physical assessment?

options.A: Wiping the stethoscope diaphragm between different patients
options.B: Reusing disposable examination gloves for a second patient
options.C: Performing hand washing after removing soiled gloves
options.D: Wearing clean gloves before palpating open skin lesions

explanation: Disposable gloves are single-use items and must never be reused across different patients. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which assessment technique involves using the sense of touch to evaluate tissue texture?
explanation: Palpation uses the hands and fingers to feel for masses, tenderness, and texture changes. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why is auscultation performed before palpation during an abdominal assessment?

options.A: To prevent the patient from falling asleep
options.B: To avoid altering natural bowel sounds
options.D: To warm up the stethoscope diaphragm

explanation: Pressing or palpating the abdomen can stimulate peristalsis, falsely increasing or changing bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h4)

question: What do anthropometric measurements primarily assess in a patient?

options.C: Electrical activity of the heart muscle

explanation: Anthropometry evaluates physical dimensions like height, weight, and limb circumferences to gauge growth and nutrition. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h5)

question: A patient presents with a sudden drop in blood pressure and a rapid pulse. What do these vital signs suggest?

options.A: An elevated basal metabolic rate due to a heavy meal
options.B: Improved cardiovascular fitness from regular exercise
options.C: Normal physiological adaptation to resting quietly
options.D: Possible circulatory compromise or fluid volume deficit

explanation: Low blood pressure paired with a fast heart rate often indicates shock, dehydration, or acute blood loss. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of using a head-to-toe approach for physical examination?

options.A: It allows the nurse to finish the exam in under two minutes
options.B: It removes the requirement for patient verbal consent
options.C: It eliminates the need to measure patient vital signs
options.D: It ensures no body system is accidentally missed

explanation: A systematic head-to-toe sequence guarantees a thorough and comprehensive assessment of the entire body. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h6)

question: A nurse examining a patient's neck during a head-to-toe assessment would typically check for what finding?

options.A: Visual acuity and pupillary light reflex
options.B: Tracheal alignment and lymph node enlargement
options.C: Bowel motility and lower quadrant tenderness
options.D: Range of motion in the ankle and knee joints

explanation: Neck assessment focuses on checking the thyroid gland, lymph nodes, and trachea position. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h6)

question: How should a nurse document physical examination findings in a patient record?

options.A: Using clear, objective, and descriptive terminology
options.B: By leaving blank spaces for other nurses to fill in
options.C: By writing down only what the patient's family says
options.D: Using vague personal opinions about the patient

explanation: Documentation must be factual, specific, and objective to maintain professional and legal standards. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h7)

question: Why is immediate verbal reporting necessary when a critical assessment finding is discovered?

options.A: To initiate rapid intervention and prevent patient deterioration
options.B: To ensure the medical record is closed before the night shift
options.C: To satisfy routine hospital auditing requirements
options.D: To reduce the total number of required nursing care plans

explanation: Critical findings require urgent communication so the healthcare team can act swiftly to stabilize the patient. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h7)
